ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure there is a relatively large rectangle ABCD, and at each of the three corners A, B, and D there is placed a small rectangle whose sides are parallel to ABCD. The thick black line represents the outer boundary after these rectangles are combined together. The center of each added rectangle is exactly on one corner of the large rectangle, so half of its width and half of its height fall near the two adjacent sides of the large rectangle, and the other part protrudes outward to form a new boundary. Reasoning: Let the width of some added rectangle be x and the height be y. When it is attached at a corner, the length of the original large rectangle boundary that is covered is x/2 + y/2; the newly added exposed boundary length is x + y + x/2 + y/2. So the net increase in boundary length brought by this rectangle is (x + y + x/2 + y/2) - (x/2 + y/2) = x + y. This value is exactly half of the perimeter 2x + 2y of this small rectangle. The sum of the perimeters of the three added rectangles is 20 cm, so they make the outer boundary increase by a total of 20/2 = 10 cm. The perimeter of the original rectangle ABCD is 30 cm, therefore the total length of the thick black line is 30 + 10 = 40 cm.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a large rectangle ABCD with three axis-parallel rectangles centered at corners A, B, and D; the thick black line is the outside boundary of the union. Let an added rectangle have width x and height y. Because its center is exactly at a corner of ABCD, half its width and half its height overlap the two sides of ABCD meeting at that corner. When this rectangle is attached, the old border loses x/2 + y/2 from the original rectangle, while the exposed new border from the added rectangle is x + y + x/2 + y/2. The net increase is therefore x + y, which is half of that added rectangle's perimeter 2x+2y. Apply this independently to the three added rectangles: total border length = perimeter of ABCD + half of the sum of the three added perimeters = 30 + 20/2 = 40 cm.
